name: Axodrine
description: Axodrine is a neuroplasticity accelerant that temporarily increases the rate of synaptic remodeling, allowing new motor programs, procedural skills, and technical knowledge to be inscribed into neural architecture in a fraction of the time normally required. Used in conjunction with BCI-delivered training simulations, it can compress weeks of skill development into days. Helix designed it for military rapid-deployment training; it has since migrated into corporate retraining programs and the gray market.
effects: Dramatically accelerated motor learning and procedural skill acquisition
Faster integration of BCI-delivered training content
Heightened neural responsiveness to practice and repetition
Increased tolerance for cognitive and physical training loads
side_effects: Existing skills can be partially overwritten if similar motor programs are trained during the active window
Severe physical and mental fatigue post-training session
Skills acquired under Axodrine are initially unstable — they degrade rapidly if not reinforced within 48 hours
Occasionally produces phantom skill-memories — the sensation of being able to do things you haven't actually trained
duration: Training window: 4-6 hours; neuroplasticity elevation persists 8-12 hours
cultural_context: Axodrine is the drug of reinvention. In a city where your economic tier is largely determined by your certified skill set, the ability to rapidly acquire new capabilities is enormously valuable. Tier 2 workers use it to attempt Tier 3 certifications. Tier 3 workers use it to stay competitive as job requirements shift. There is an entire underground industry of 'accelerated credential mills' — unlicensed training facilities that pair Axodrine with pirated BCI training programs and promise new professional certifications in a week. The skill instability problem means many of these credentials are fragile — workers who trained under Axodrine without proper reinforcement find their abilities beginning to erode under real-world conditions.
story_hooks: A credential mill on the Tier 1-2 border has been selling accelerated surgical certifications — people are performing medical procedures with Axodrine-acquired skills that were never properly reinforced, and the complication rate is climbing.

A player character needs a specific skill set urgently — a contact can get them Axodrine and a BCI training package, but the skill will be unstable without follow-up practice they may not have time for.

Someone has figured out how to use Axodrine's skill-overwrite effect deliberately — a fixer is offering a service that erases specific trained behaviors from targets, a kind of pharmaceutical reprogramming that is deeply illegal and deeply in demand.
